questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
One of the key factors in choosing my study destination was Australia’s unique and diverse agriculture.
The country has completely different climatic conditions, crops, and production systems compared to what I’m familiar with in Denmark, which provides me with a new and valuable perspective for my studies. Additionally, it was important for me to experience a different culture and the distinctive wildlife, which have both played a significant role in my academic and personal development.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I truly enjoyed my time abroad, and I would highly recommend the experience to others.
It has helped me build a broad network and gain a wider perspective on environmental issues, sustainability, and cultural challenges—both globally and locally.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It has been relatively easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of help from the Learning Abroad team. They were able to assist with everything from housing and jobs to course selection and even the small details.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
I have been very satisfied. I felt safe and supported throughout the entire process.
In addition, there were some great activities organized by the Learning Abroad team that made it easy to meet both other exchange students and local students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On campus, there was the option to live in single rooms or in apartments where six people shared a kitchen, living room, and bathrooms, but each person had their own bedroom. That’s where I lived, and it was located about 100–200 meters from campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We cooked our own meals in the apartment. Additionally, there was a free brunch every Saturday, and on some days during the week, you could buy a meal for 5 dollars to have for dinner.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I have really enjoyed living on campus, as it is close to the university and many other students. Living with six people in an apartment worked really well. The rooms are a good size, and there are good facilities for cooking, relaxing in the living room, and beautiful nature behind the campus.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was simple and easy to navigate.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Learning Abroad team was extremely supportive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy to register for and deregister from courses. I received help with changing courses from the Learning Abroad team, and they were really good at assisting me. I spent about an hour with someone from the Learning Abroad team to sort out my courses, as several of them were in the same schedule group.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the Learning Abroad team. If they can’t help you, they know who else you should get in touch with.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think they offered some good courses, but the quality of the teaching varied. There was a lot of online material to watch or read, and only a few hours where you were physically present.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2 first-year courses and 2 second-year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching involved a lot of online material and few hours of physical attendance in some courses. Often consisted of recorded PowerPoint presentations and discussions or exercises related to the material when meeting physically. In courses with laboratory and fieldwork, there were more in-person sessions where attendance was required.  I think it worked quite well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
KLA115	Sustainable Resource Management
KLA255	Introductory Entomology and Plant Pathology
KPA214	Plants in Action
KSA101	Introduction to Marine and Antarctic Science A

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course KLA115 Sustainable Resource Management, as it is a very broad course that covers many of the sustainability and environmental challenges Australia faces, while also providing a global perspective. The courses Plants in Action and Introductory Entomology and Plant Pathology were also very good, with many practical exercises such as insect collection and nutrient experiments with various plants.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I chose to buy a car while I was there, so I had quite a few expenses related to that. Additionally, I also had to purchase a lab coat.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables were a bit more expensive than expected, but otherwise most things were priced about the same or slightly higher than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can participate in almost anything, and there are also academic clubs where you have the chance to meet people who share your interests. There were really many opportunities to experience things together with other students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you could think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going on many excursions. There are great opportunities for camping and hiking, which allow you to get out into nature and experience Tasmania’s wild landscapes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on many excursions. There are great opportunities for camping and hiking, which allow you to get out into nature and experience Tasmania’s wild landscapes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adapt. People are very hospitable and have a great understanding of exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the language, as there was a bit of slang.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it is a country area, so it was great to see rodeo and the Australian style of agriculture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Consider getting a car, as there are no trains or buses that go out to the beautiful nature areas. It gives you great freedom to explore the whole island during holidays and weekends. I really enjoyed living in a 6-person apartment because there was plenty of space, and you get to know the people you live with. Be patient when learning their school system, and everything will work out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Definitely live on campus. It’s very social, and it’s easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature, the people, and diving – I got my diving certification there, which I highly recommend because of the beautiful marine life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had some difficulty understanding everything because my English wasn’t very strong, but it got better and better.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I am very grateful for my stay and will definitely visit Tasmania again. It is the most beautiful place I have ever been.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
